findings.claim: Pizza Margherita, Country Sourdough Loaf and Baguette de Tradition all rest on fermentation and the pause that does the work
findings.because: The brief lists "Resting dough: the pause that does the work" on Pizza Margherita and Country Sourdough Loaf only; Baguette de Tradition's techniques are Fermentation, Proofing and Steaming. "All" attributes a technique to the baguette that the app does not place on it.
findings.fix: Pizza Margherita, Country Sourdough Loaf and Baguette de Tradition all rest on fermentation; the pizza and the loaf add resting dough, the pause that does the work

findings.claim: the loaf and the baguette add steaming under basket, leaf and lid
findings.because: "Steaming: basket, leaf and lid" is the technique's title in the app, not how a loaf is steamed. No baguette or country loaf is steamed under a basket or a leaf: a baguette bakes with steam in the oven (a tray of water or injected steam) and a country loaf under a lidded pot's trapped moisture, so the crust stays soft long enough for oven spring before it sets. As written a cook would look for a leaf.
findings.fix: the loaf and the baguette add steaming, the moisture in the oven that lets the crust spring before it sets

findings.claim: so the half hour is all cooking and the real work is the prep before the flame
findings.because: Self-contradicting and reversed. In a 30-minute char kway teow the flame time is two or three minutes per small batch; the rest of the half hour is the mise (noodles loosened, lap cheong sliced, prawns cleaned, chives cut, sauce mixed). The semester's own line says total mise and small batches: prep is most of the clock, not outside it.
findings.fix: so most of the half hour is mise and the cooking itself is minutes per batch

findings.claim: Log each dish the day you cook it; when all seven are logged, the Level test at the foot of the page is untimed and ends on what you missed with the right answers.
findings.because: "when all seven are logged" reads as a condition on sitting the test, which the brief does not set: nothing is locked, and the levelTest line describes the test with no gate. A cook at this level would wait to take it.
findings.fix: Log each dish the day you cook it; the Level test at the foot of the page is untimed and ends on what you missed with the right answers.

findings.claim: all rest on fermentation and the pause that does the work: flour, water, salt, time. Pizza and the baguette add proofing, the rise before the oven;

findings.fix: all rest on fermentation: flour, water, salt, time. Pizza and the loaf add resting dough, the pause that does the work; pizza and the baguette add proofing, the rise before the oven;

findings.fix: The Level test at the foot of the page is untimed, runs across the subsections and ends on what you missed with the right answers.

findings.claim: Low & slow smoking is the same fire on a longer timer
findings.because: The brief's own definition for this item opens "Three fires, three clocks": grilling is direct high heat for minutes on tender cuts; barbecue is indirect low heat plus wood smoke for hours on collagen cuts (brisket, shoulder, ribs). It is a different fire, a different heat path and a different cut, not the grill left running longer; a sous who reads it as the same fire will set up a direct, hot bed and get the standard's fault.
findings.fix: Low & slow smoking is a different fire: indirect, low, fed with wood smoke, for collagen cuts on a clock of hours:

findings.claim: the egg white, cornstarch and soda coat that gives stir-fried meat its silk
findings.because: The brief's definition says the coat is egg white, cornstarch "and a little baking soda or wine", rested, "then pre-cooked briefly in oil or water". Classic velveting uses rice wine; soda is one option, not the rule, and the brief pass through oil or water before the wok is the step that makes velveting velveting. Naming soda as fixed and dropping the pre-cook teaches the technique wrong.
findings.fix: the egg white and cornstarch coat with a little soda or wine, rested and passed briefly through oil or water before the wok, that gives stir-fried meat its silk

findings.claim: take them once the grill standard is in your hands

findings.fix: Cobia is fattier than most white fish, firm and buttery, and often goes out raw as crudo.

findings.fix: Salt takes the bitterness down, sweetness buffers it and fat rounds it off; only acid leaves the edge in place and brightens past it.
